name: AMORDEGRC
description: AMORDEGRC returns the depreciation of an asset for a given period based on a depreciation coefficient used in French accounting.
tldr: Calculates depreciation for a specific period using the French declining balance method.

parameters.name: first_period
parameters.description: End date of the first period.

parameters.name: salvage
parameters.description: Salvage value at the end of the asset life.

parameters.name: period
parameters.description: Period for which to calculate depreciation.

basicExample.explanation: Calculates first-year depreciation for a $10,000 asset with a 20% depreciation rate.

advancedExamples.title: With actual year basis
advancedExamples.explanation: Basis 1 uses actual days for the period.

howItWorks: AMORDEGRC applies a depreciation coefficient based on the asset life and calculates declining balance depreciation. It is used primarily in French accounting systems.

howToSteps.name: Calculate
howToSteps.text: Press Enter to get the result.

limitations: Used mainly in French accounting standards.
Rate is determined by asset life and a coefficient table.
Basis determines how days are counted.

commonErrors.cause: Rate does not match the French coefficient for the asset life.
commonErrors.fix: Use the correct coefficient based on asset life.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: AMORDEGRC works identically in Google Sheets.
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: Same syntax and behavior as Excel.

faq.question: What is the difference between AMORDEGRC and AMORLINC?
faq.answer: AMORDEGRC uses declining balance. AMORLINC uses straight-line depreciation.

faq.question: When is AMORDEGRC used?
faq.answer: It is used in French accounting for accelerated depreciation.
